---
title: "Sacrificial Debt"
---

This subsite is a **generated research publication surface** for the Sacrificial Debt project. Canonical evidence remains in the versioned workbench records.

The project asks when perceived exemption from collective sacrifice can become an attributed political debt and under what additional conditions that debt becomes essentialized, non-dischargeable, or coercively collected.

::: {.callout-warning}
The workbench treats perpetrator rhetoric as historical evidence, not as valid moral justification. Sacrificial Debt is a mechanism to test and delimit, not a total explanation of genocide or political violence.
:::

## Project Documents

### [Research Program Prospectus](prospectus/)

The prospectus defines Sacrificial Debt as a comparative theory-building research program. It records the central research question, case-comparison logic, falsification burden, and staged relationship between the broader program and the first empirical paper.

### [Pilot Status](status/)

The status page summarizes what the manual pilot has stabilized, what remains
provisional, what is not yet evidence, and what would weaken early claims.
